title: An obligation in one place, a definition in another
kind: The Drift Layer, paper no. 6 — Version 1
summary: Confirmation of Payee puts the duty in a regulator's direction and the content of the check in a rule book someone else maintains. What a later instrument would have to add.

title: A liability rule aimed at the wrong control: what the law offers when a delegate exceeds its instruction
kind: The Drift Layer, paper no. 5 — Version 1
summary: A reading of Part 7 of the Payment Services Regulations 2017 and of the common-law ledger, applied to a payment executed by a software delegate under a standing instruction: which provisions can and cannot reach the case where the close is outside the description the payer gave.

title: The Drift Layer: the clean, fast session that is not proof of authority
kind: The Drift Layer, paper no. 4 — Version 1
summary: Merchant-side friction models lean on proxies for a human nervous system: hesitation, mouse movement, repeated clicks, typos, abandonment. What those signals are worth when there is no nervous system behind the session.

title: Response to HM Treasury, Modernising Payment Services Regulation
summary: Submitted response to the HM Treasury consultation, answering questions 15 to 18 and 42.

title: Four Measures for Mandate Conformance
summary: Evaluation coverage, mandate conformance, divergence incidence, and unauthorised continuation. Coverage is reported first. Version 2 corrects defects found by computing the measures from the Version 1 wording alone; Version 1 is retained and citable. The definitions are free and citable, and stay that way.

title: Response to the Bank of England, RPIB consultation on the design of future retail payments infrastructure
summary: Submitted response to the Bank of England consultation on the design of future retail payments infrastructure.
